questions.question: In Node's error-first callback convention, what is the first argument passed to the callback?
options: An error object, or null when the operation succeeded
The name of the function that was called
questions.explanation: Error-first callbacks receive (err, result). The code must check err before using the result, and usually return after handling the error.

questions.question: You need to send 50 notification emails and report which ones failed, without stopping at the first failure. Which combinator fits best?
questions.explanation: Promise.allSettled waits for every promise and returns a status object for each, so you can see all successes and failures. Promise.all rejects on the first failure.

questions.question: Why is `const a = await getUser(); const b = await getOrders();` slower than it needs to be when the two calls are independent?
options: The second call does not start until the first finishes; Promise.all would run them concurrently
await blocks the whole event loop
await converts the calls into synchronous file reads
It is not slower; both forms take the same time
questions.explanation: Sequential awaits serialise the operations. Starting both and awaiting Promise.all([getUser(), getOrders()]) lets them overlap. await pauses only the current async function, not the loop.

questions.question: What is the simplest built-in way to make a fetch call give up after 3 seconds?
questions.explanation: AbortSignal.timeout(ms) returns a signal that aborts automatically after the delay, and fetch accepts it through the signal option.
